before: Created the Arkansas Data Centers Act of 2023 for digital asset mining; allowed digital asset mining in industrial-zoned areas not designated by the local government for other use; barred local requirements that treated mining businesses differently from data centers.
after: As enacted in 2023, the Arkansas Data Centers Act addressed digital asset mining; it allowed qualifying mining businesses in industrial-zoned areas not designated for other uses and limited local requirements that treated mining businesses differently from data centers. Acts 173 and 174 of 2024 later amended the framework; current law requires separate verification.
Enacted as Act 373, approved and effective 2025-03-20

before: Created the Generating Arkansas Jobs Act of 2025; authorized strategic utility investment recovery and accelerated review of major utility facilities, including a six-month review period cited by state officials as supporting data center load growth.
after: Act 373 created the Generating Arkansas Jobs Act of 2025, authorizing strategic utility investment recovery and conditional certificate procedures, including a six-month deadline when the commission determines a certificate is in the public interest. The existing attribution to state officials linking the law to data-center load growth remains unverified in the retained sources.

before: Enacted as Act 173 (SB78) and Act 174 (SB79), both act-dated 2024-05-03
after: Acts 173 and 174 approved and effective 2024-05-03; legislative notifications 2024-05-09

before: Reworked crypto-mining regulation after local complaints; Association of Arkansas Counties reports Act 173 repealed limits on local noise and zoning controls, while Act 174 created an Arkansas Oil and Gas Commission permitting process for crypto mining.
after: In 2024 Act 173 added noise-reduction requirements for covered digital asset mining businesses and barred local ordinances prohibiting or requiring prior approval for home mining. Acts 173 and 174 each amended the earlier local restrictions, removing specified limits on home-mining noise rules, differential business requirements, and discriminatory rezoning while retaining a prohibition on rezoning without compliance with applicable law. Act 174 created state permitting for covered mining businesses with an initial-rules transition and preserved consistent local regulation in areas not otherwise addressed. Both addressed prohibited foreign ownership. Later amendments and current force remain unverified.
adjudication: revised to reflect visual inspection of both acts

after: SR7–SR12 failed third-reading votes 2026-04-21 and died at sine die 2026-04-29; HR1010–HR1015 died in House committee 2026-04-29. after: The listed resolutions sought authorization for nonappropriation bills on crypto-mining local control, extraordinary electricity-use fees, foreign hardware/software restrictions, amendments to money-services law, advance notice before land acquisition or construction, and water-use and electric-grid impacts.
